characteristics.cultivar: Camellia sinensis var. sinensis and hybrids

description.short: Gentle, softly sweet black tea cultivated at high altitudes in India's southernmost state
description.overview: Nestled in the Cardamom Hills of Kerala, Munnar is famed not only for fragrant tea but also for cardamoms cultivated alongside tea estates on dramatic mist-shrouded mountain slopes.
description.taste: Smooth, well-balanced, rounded with gentle sweetness and low astringency
description.processing: Plucking → withering → rolling → full oxidation → drying

history.origin: Estates were pioneered by Scottish planters in the late 19th century who expanded into the cool highlands of southern India following earlier tea successes in the north.
history.development: The region historically produced aromatic cardamom spice alongside tea shrubs, giving rise to the name of the surrounding Cardamom Hills mountain range.
history.modern: Today, Munnar serves as a hub of both plantation agriculture and scenic eco-tourism, featuring colonial heritage bungalows and tea history museums.
interestingFacts: The Cardamom Hills take their name from the aromatic spice naturally flourishing alongside the hill stations' tea gardens.
Munnar is one of India's premier tourist destinations, celebrated for panoramic emerald tea hills that blanket the peaks.
